9. Transaction Processing

sections.heading: 9. Transaction Processing

blocks.text: An ICL file can contain one or more cash letters for deposit to the Client’s Account(s) with Bank. Cash letters must contain check detail records and the associated image records. ICLs must be sent to Bank prior to the agreed-upon processing deadline. An ICL has been sent to Bank only when the entire file has been transmitted and delivered to Bank in an agreed-upon format that satisfies image quality standards. Based on the size of the file, there may be a significant delay between the start and the completion of the file transmission. As a result, every effort should be made to send ICL files as early as possible. Files that are received by Bank after a deposit deadline will be considered deposited for the next deposit deadline period. For purposes of determining when an item has been delivered and received, Bank’s records shall be determinative. Processing fees and funds availability will be assessed based on the deposit deadline that is met. Problems with hardware, software, or data transmission may on occasion delay or prevent Bank from receiving files or other data electronically. Accordingly, Client should have a contingency plan to send any ICL files or other data by other means should such a circumstance arise.

These Terms and Conditions provide information on the use of the Zero Balance Account (“ZBA”) Service described below.
1. Description of Service

sections.heading: 1. Description of Service

blocks.text: The ZBA Service allows Client to manage its daily cash flows by consolidating balances from multiple zero balance or subsidiary accounts into a single master account. Client shall designate a master Account (“Master Account”) to be used in conjunction with one or more sub-Account(s) (“Sub-Account(s)”) to concentrate deposits into the Master Account or fund multiple disbursing Sub-Account(s) from the Master Account.

    with one or more sub-Account(s) (“Sub-Account(s)”) to concentrate deposits into the Master Account or fund multiple disbursing

2. Daily Posting and Funding

sections.heading: 2. Daily Posting and Funding

blocks.text: Checks can be written or deposits made to the Sub-Account or the Master Account. Funds are automatically transferred from the Master Account to cover the exact amount of net debits to any Sub-Account(s), including any target ledger balance at the end of posting on each Business Day as designated by Client from time to time (“Target Balance”). In the event there is a net credit in the Sub-Account(s) above the Target Balance, if any, at the close of each Business Day, the credit balance of such Sub-Account shall automatically be transferred to the Master Account.

        able at or through banks located outside the United States (“Foreign Items”) and to receive provisional credit from Bank for same;
        WHEREAS, Bank has advised Customer that processing, transportation, clearing and return of Foreign Items takes more time generally
        and also poses a higher risk of error or delay than with respect to domestic items; and
        WHEREAS, to induce Bank to accept Foreign Items for deposit, Customer is willing to assume such risks and hold Bank harmless.
        NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which
        are hereby acknowledged, Bank and Customer hereby agree as follows:
1. Bank establishes clearing arrangements from time to time with foreign banks for the clearing of Foreign Items drawn on or payable at
                 or through foreign bank offices located in certain foreign countries. The list of such countries may change from time to time without
                 notice to Customer. In the event Customer deposits any Foreign Item drawn on or payable at or through a foreign bank office located in
                 a country in which Bank does not at that time undertake to clear Foreign Items (or Customer deposits any Foreign Item which is unac-
                 ceptable to Bank for any other reason), Bank will reverse any credit made to Customer’s account with respect to such Foreign Item and
                 return such Foreign Item to Customer or advise Customer to pick up same (which Customer shall do within a reasonable time).
2. Banks located outside the United States generally are not subject to the check clearing laws, regulations, and customs in effect in
                 the United States (such as the Uniform Commercial Code or Federal Reserve Board Regulations CC or J), which require domestic
                 drawee banks either to make final payment or promptly return domestic items in an expeditious manner. In addition, the processing,
                 transportation, clearing and return of Foreign Items takes more time (often a long time) and relies on manual handling, which is
                 prone to a higher incidence of delay or other errors compared to domestic items, for which processing is substantially facilitated by
                 computers. Customer understands that credit given for deposit of Foreign Items may remain provisional and subject to reversal for
                 a long and indefinite period of time; that Bank cannot determine with certainty a date after which any settlement which Bank has
                 received for a Foreign Item from a foreign clearing or drawee bank will become final and not subject to reversal (thereby result-
                 ing in reversal of provisional credit given by Bank to Customer and that Bank will not be bound by any statement alleged to have
                 been made to Customer by any Bank employee to the effect that a Foreign Item has been finally paid, finally collected, or the like.
                 Notwithstanding the higher risks associated with Foreign Items, Customer desires to deposit Foreign Items to Customer’s account(s)
                 with Bank. In order to induce Bank to accept such deposits, Customer agrees to assume the risk of delays and other errors, as well
                 as the risk that credit given to Customer will be reversed, or reimbursement demanded by Bank from Customer, longer after such
                 deposit was made, and Customer agrees to hold Bank harmless from losses and expenses incurred by Customer arising out of or in
                 connection with Foreign Items, except as otherwise specifically provided to the contrary in Section 5 below.

      Triggering Event. The Triggering Event for a Program Withdrawal is a net change in your Root Account balance, after
      the posting of all your Root Account activity for a Business Day, that causes it (exclusive of any amounts that we credit

      Return Amount. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, if such a Triggering Event occurs, we will transfer
      an amount from the Deposit Accounts at ICS Settlement on the next Business Day, up to the available amount in the
      Deposit Accounts, sufficient to restore your Root Account balance to the Target Balance.
           (b) Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, and subject to the rules and cutoff times that otherwise
      apply to root accounts with us, we will honor your debit transactions in the Root Account so long as the sum of your Root
      Account balance and your balance in the Deposit Accounts of the applicable type, after taking into account any pending
      Program Deposits and any pending Program Withdrawals, is not less than zero. We will do so even if the amount of the

1. Pursuant to this Agreement, you authorize us to hold and act as your custodian with respect to all deposit
      accounts, including all time deposits, money market deposit accounts, and demand deposit accounts, issued or
      established pursuant to the CDARS Deposit Placement Agreement, the ICS Deposit Placement Agreement, or a
      predecessor agreement (“Deposit Accounts”) for funds of yours placed as deposits through CDARS®, the Certificate of
      Deposit Account Registry Service®, or ICS, the IntraFi® Cash Service, and all your security entitlements and other related
      interests and assets with respect to the Deposit Accounts (“Related Entitlements”). The custodial account in which we
      will hold the Deposit Accounts and Related Entitlements (“Custodial Account”) comprises all the CDARS and ICS
      custodial accounts that we maintain for you.
2. As your custodian, we may (i) cause the Deposit Accounts to be titled in our name or in the name of our sub-
      custodian, (ii) collect for your account all interest and other payments of income or principal pertaining to the Deposit
      Accounts, (iii) endorse on your behalf any check or other instrument received for your account that requires endorsement,
      (iv) in accordance with your instructions, deposit your funds in, or withdraw your funds from, the Deposit Accounts, (v)
      in accordance with your instructions, deliver or transfer funds from another account with us to the Deposit Accounts or
      deliver or transfer funds from the Deposit Accounts to another account with us, (vi) for Deposit Accounts that are time
      deposits, surrender for payment for your account maturing CDs and those for which early withdrawal is requested, (vii)
      execute and deliver or file on your behalf all appropriate receipts and releases and other instruments, including whatever
      certificates may be required from custodians or may be necessary to obtain exemption from taxes and to name you
      when required for the purpose of the instrument, and (viii) take such other actions as are customary or necessary to
      effectuate the purposes of this Agreement.
3. For purposes of Article 8 of the Uniform Commercial Code in applicable state law (“UCC”), we will act as your
      securities intermediary for, and will treat as financial assets, any Deposit Accounts and Related Entitlements that we
      hold for you pursuant to this Agreement. The Custodial Account will be a securities account, as defined in the UCC.
4. We may comply with any writ of attachment, execution, garnishment, tax levy, restraining order, subpoena,
      warrant, or other legal process that we believe (correctly or otherwise) to be valid. We may notify you of such process
      by telephone, electronically, or in writing. If we are not fully reimbursed for records research, imaging, photocopying,
      and handling costs by the party that served the process, we may charge such costs to your account, in addition to any
      minimum fee we charge for complying with legal processes.
5. We may honor any legal process that is served personally, by mail, or by electronic mail or facsimile transmission
      at any of our offices or an office of our agent (including locations other than where the funds, records, or property sought
      is held), even if the law requires personal delivery at the office where your account or records are maintained.
6. We will have no liability to you for any good-faith act or omission by us in connection with this Agreement. You
      agree to indemnify us and our sub-custodian, and to hold us and our sub-custodian harmless from, all expenses

   The Account Holder(s) (herein called ‘Depositor’) have agreed to use the night depository facilities of First Horizon Bank (herein
   called ‘the Bank’) for safekeeping services in accordance with the terms and conditions contained in this agreement.
         • If keys are provided to Depositor for access to the night depository, you agree not to duplicate them and to return them to the
           Bank on termination of this agreement.
         • Depositor should use disposable tamper-evident bags for making deposits (herein called ‘night deposit bags’). Depositor
           agrees that night deposit bags must be properly sealed with the account name and number clearly indicated on the outside
           of the bag. Depositor agrees that if both safekeeping (not processed) and regular (to be processed) night deposit bags are
           dropped that any safekeeping bags will be clearly marked as such. Any bag found to be unsealed, damaged, or improperly
           labeled will be opened and processed. Depositor agrees that each bag placed in the night depository facility shall contain
           nothing other than currency, coin and negotiable paper owned by Depositor along with an itemized deposit slip for the
           enclosures. Depositor further agrees to verify that the bag has cleared the night depository entry chute prior to leaving the
           premises. Depositor agrees not to allow any unauthorized person to use the night depository facility or have possession of
           the key, if applicable, to the night depository facility.
         • Depositor authorizes the Bank to take possession of safekeeping night deposit bags placed in the night deposit facility and to
           hold such bags, without processing, on behalf of Depositor.
         • Depositor shall pick up any safekeeping bags by the business day following deposit.
         • Depositor agrees that the use of the night depository facility shall be at the Depositor’s sole risk, and Depositor assumes any
           and all risks incidental to or arising out of the operation or use of the night depository facility. In the absence of prior actual
           knowledge of a defect, neither the Bank nor any of its agents shall be liable for any loss or damage sustained by Depositor in
           the use of said facility which results from an Act of God, mechanical defect or malfunctioning of the facility itself, the keys,
           locks, bags or other equipment sold, loaned, or used in connection therewith; or Depositor’s inability to properly operate the
           night depository facility; or the deposit of property other than currency, coin and negotiable paper unless such damages or
           loss are caused by, and there is affirmative evidence of, the Bank’s failure to exercise reasonable and ordinary care. Depositor
           further expressly agrees that the Bank will not be responsible for any loss or damage sustained by Depositor caused by the
           use of the night depository facilities by any of the Bank’s other customers or any other persons for any dangerous or unlawful
           purposes, or arising from acts of vandalism, malicious mischief, or criminal acts, including but not limited to larceny, robbery,
           or breaking and entering.
         • Depositor’s right to use the night depository facility shall not be transferable by Depositor without the written consent of the
           Bank, and the Bank reserves the right to amend, revoke, or terminate this Agreement at any time. If such amendments are
           unacceptable to Depositor, Depositor may terminate this Agreement by giving written notice of termination to the Bank. The
           Bank may temporarily suspend use of the night depository, without any resulting liability, by posting a sign to that effect at or
           near the night depository in the event of an emergency or to make alterations or repairs.
         • This Night Depository Agreement is governed by and subject to all applicable federal laws and all applicable substantive laws
           of the state in which we are located and where you opened your account.

sections.heading: Security Features

blocks.text: You must choose one of these security features that will apply to all phone-initiated outgoing wire transfers. The individual Confirming/Approving the wire must provide a valid PIN with limits equal to or exceeding the dollar amount of the wire.

     Callback verification on all wire transfers

sections.heading: Callback verification on all wire transfers

blocks.text: • This feature will require a second PIN verification on all wire transfers regardless of amount. A Bank Representative will place a call to one of the Confirmers/Approvers listed in the Telephone Wire Authorization section. The Confirmers/Approvers must furnish their PIN before the Bank will transfer any amount of funds. Callback verification on wire transfers over specified dollar limits. • This feature will require a second PIN verification on a per wire basis according to the dollar amount and type of wire (nonrepetitive and repetitive). Dollar limits are defined by wire type. Only wires over the defined dollar limit will require a second PIN verification. A Bank Representative will place a call to one of the Confirmers/Approvers listed in the Telephone Wire Authorization section. The Confirmers/Approvers must furnish their PIN before the Bank will transfer funds over the specified dollar limits.

     Callback verification on wire transfers over specified dollar limits.
      • This feature will require a second PIN verification on a per wire basis according to the dollar amount and type of wire (nonrepetitive and repetitive). Dollar limits are defined by wire
        type. Only wires over the defined dollar limit will require a second PIN verification. A Bank Representative will place a call to one of the Confirmers/Approvers listed in the Telephone
        Wire Authorization section. The Confirmers/Approvers must furnish their PIN before the Bank will transfer funds over the specified dollar limits.
     Important

sections.heading: Important

blocks.text: • The Confirmers’ dollar limit must equal or exceed the dollar amount of the wire in order for the wire to be released. • If a second PIN verification cannot be obtained by 5:30 p.m. ET, the wire will not be released. The next business day, a Bank Representative will attempt to contact the person who initiated the wire to obtain further instructions. • If callback verification on wire transfers over specified dollar limits is checked and dollar amounts are not entered, all wires will require a second PIN verification. • The individual Confirming/Approving the wire must provide a valid PIN with limits equal to or exceeding the dollar amount of the wire.

sections.heading: Telephone Security Features

blocks.text: Callback Verification with a Second PIN for Outgoing WIRES • The Bank may require verification of wire transfers depending on type of transfer and dollar amount. Regardless of the verification option selected, the Bank will continue to verify some transfers. However, because these verification procedures may change at any time without notice, specific requirements can be established by selecting one of the verification options. • If funds are frequently transferred from the same account to the same destination bank and beneficiary, a unique identifier name or code for these transactions can be assigned (called templates/repetitive wire transfer or repetitive wire transfers or template wires), thus eliminating callers from repeating all information for each transfer. The dollar amount of each repetitive or template transfer may vary. • You will have the opportunity to set up repetitive or template wires in the section of this Set-up Form for Repetitive/Templates Wire.

sections.text:
What is this form?
        To help the government fight financial crime, Federal regulation requires certain financial institutions to
        obtain, verify, and record information about the beneficial owners of legal entity customers.
        Who has to complete this form?
        This form must be completed by the person opening a new account on behalf of a legal entity with any of the
        following U.S. financial institutions: a bank or credit union; a broker or dealer in securities; a mutual fund; a
        futures commission merchant; or an introducing broker in commodities.
        For the purposes of this form, a legal entity includes a corporation, limited liability company, or other entity
        that is created by a filing of a public document with a Secretary of State or similar office, a general
        partnership, and any similar business entity formed in the United States or a foreign country. Legal entity
        does not include a sole proprietorship, an unincorporated association, a natural person opening accounts on
        their own behalf, or a U.S. state or local government entity.
        What information do I have to provide?
        This form requires you to provide the name, address, date of birth, and Social Security number (or passport
        number or other similar information, in the case of non-U.S. persons) for the following individuals (i.e., the
        beneficial owners):
            (i)    Equity Owners: Each individual, if any, who owns, directly or indirectly, a select percentage or more of the equity
                   interests of the legal entity:
                   FHN will utilize 25% as the "select" percentage with the exception of the following:
                     Southeast Florida Market - 10% ownership

sections.heading: Southeast Florida Market - 10% ownership

blocks.text: Foreign Business entities in all markets - 10% ownership Domestic Business entities with 50% or more foreign ownership in all markets - 10% ownership (ii) Control Person: An individual with significant responsibility for managing the legal entity customer (e.g., a Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Managing Member, General Partner, President, Vice President, Secretary or Treasurer). The number of individuals that satisfy this definition of "Beneficial Owner" may vary. Under section (i - Equity Owners), depending on the factual circumstances, up to ten individuals (but as few as zero) may need to be identified. Regardless of the number of "Equity Owner" individuals identified under section (i), you must provide the identifying information of one Control Person under section (ii). It is possible that in some circumstances the same individual might be identified under both sections (e.g., the President of Acme, Inc., who also holds a 25% equity interest). A completed form will contain the identifying information of at least one individual (under section (ii - Control Person), and up to ten individuals under section (i - Equity Owners)). Note: Certain legal entity types must provide information only for a control person (an individual with significant responsibility (as described at ii, above), including (1) any legal entity that is established as a nonprofit corporation/not for profit or similar entity (like a non-profit, church or charity) and has filed its organizational documents with the appropriate State authority as necessary, and

For Business Accounts, other Acceptable Payees, covered by this agreement:
        This Foreign Items Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made this                         day of                     ,       between First Horizon
        Bank (“Bank”), and                                     (“Customer”).
        WHEREAS, Customer desires to include in deposits to its account(s) with Bank Checks or other cash items which are drawn on or pay-
        able at or through banks located outside the United States (“Foreign Items”) and to receive provisional credit from Bank for same;
        WHEREAS, Bank has advised Customer that processing, transportation, clearing and return of Foreign Items takes more time generally
        and also poses a higher risk of error or delay than with respect to domestic items; and
        WHEREAS, to induce Bank to accept Foreign Items for deposit, Customer is willing to assume such risks and hold Bank harmless.
        NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and adequacy of which
        are hereby acknowledged, Bank and Customer hereby agree as follows:
1. Bank establishes clearing arrangements from time to time with foreign banks for the clearing of Foreign Items drawn on or payable at
                 or through foreign bank offices located in certain foreign countries. The list of such countries may change from time to time without
                 notice to Customer. In the event Customer deposits any Foreign Item drawn on or payable at or through a foreign bank office located in
                 a country in which Bank does not at that time undertake to clear Foreign Items (or Customer deposits any Foreign Item which is unac-
                 ceptable to Bank for any other reason), Bank will reverse any credit made to Customer’s account with respect to such Foreign Item and
                 return such Foreign Item to Customer or advise Customer to pick up same (which Customer shall do within a reasonable time).
2. Banks located outside the United States generally are not subject to the check clearing laws, regulations, and customs in effect in
                 the United States (such as the Uniform Commercial Code or Federal Reserve Board Regulations CC or J), which require domestic
                 drawee banks either to make final payment or promptly return domestic items in an expeditious manner. In addition, the processing,
                 transportation, clearing and return of Foreign Items takes more time (often a long time) and relies on manual handling, which is
                 prone to a higher incidence of delay or other errors compared to domestic items, for which processing is substantially facilitated by
                 computers. Customer understands that credit given for deposit of Foreign Items may remain provisional and subject to reversal for
                 a long and indefinite period of time; that Bank cannot determine with certainty a date after which any settlement which Bank has
                 received for a Foreign Item from a foreign clearing or drawee bank will become final and not subject to reversal (thereby result-
                 ing in reversal of provisional credit given by Bank to Customer and that Bank will not be bound by any statement alleged to have

After posting all your Root Account activity for a Business Day, we will determine whether your Root Account balance exceeds the Target Balance by more than the Minimum Sweep Amount. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, if such a Triggering Event occurs, we will transfer the amount by which your Root Account balance exceeds the Target Balance to the Deposit Accounts at ICS Settlement on the next Business Day. blocks.text: (a) All Program Withdrawals will be Regular Program Withdrawals, which occur on the Business Day following the Triggering Event. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, if such a Triggering Event occurs, we will transfer an amount from the Deposit Accounts at ICS Settlement on the next Business Day, up to the available amount in the Deposit Accounts, sufficient to restore your Root Account balance to the Target Balance. sections.heading: Callback verification on all wire transfers

blocks.text: • This feature will require a second PIN verification on all wire transfers regardless of amount. A Bank Representative will place a call to one of the Confirmers/Approvers listed in the Telephone Wire Authorization section.
